records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣א יוֹסֵף֮ וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לְפַרְעֹה֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אָבִ֨י וְאַחַ֜י וְצֹאנָ֤ם וּבְקָרָם֙ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָהֶ֔ם בָּ֖אוּ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וְהִנָּ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ גֹּֽשֶׁן׃
records.gloss: And came Joseph and told Pharaoh and said, my father and my brothers and their flocks and their herds and all that [is] to them have come from [the] land of Canaan, and here they [are] in [the] land of Goshen.
pieces: Joseph went in to Pharaoh with the news. "My father and brothers have come from Canaan with their sheep and goats, their cattle, and all they own. At this moment they are in the land of Goshen."

L.1: Then Joseph went in and told Pharaoh, "My father and my brothers, with their flocks and their herds and all that they have, have come from the land of Canaan, and see, they are in the land of Goshen."

R.1: Joseph went to Pharaoh and told him, "My father and my brothers have come from Canaan. They brought their flocks and herds and everything they own. They are in Goshen now."

decisions.choice: they are in Goshen: a request prepared
decisions.reason: Joseph tells Pharaoh where his family already is. He does not yet ask for the land, but he prepares the way for the brothers' request in verse 4.

decisions.choice: sheep and goats
decisions.reason: Tson means a flock of small animals, sheep and goats together.

records.source: וּמִקְצֵ֣ה אֶחָ֔יו לָקַ֖ח חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּצִּגֵ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And from [the] end of his brothers he took five men and presented them before Pharaoh.
pieces: He had brought five of his brothers with him, and he presented them to Pharaoh.

L.2: And from among his brothers he took five men and presented them to Pharaoh.

R.2: Joseph took five of his brothers with him and brought them to meet Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: from the end of his brothers: from among his brothers
alternatives: from the whole number of his brothers
decisions.reason: Miqtseh, "from the end", here means "from among" or "out of the whole group". It does not say which five, or that they were the weakest or strongest.

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֛ה אֶל־אֶחָ֖יו מַה־מַּעֲשֵׂיכֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֗ה רֹעֵ֥ה צֹאן֙ עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ גַּם־אֲנַ֖חְנוּ גַּם־אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Pharaoh to his brothers, what [are] your occupations? And they said to Pharaoh, shepherds of flock [are] your servants, both we and our fathers.
pieces: Pharaoh asked Joseph's brothers, "What do you do?" They replied, "Your servants keep flocks, as our fathers did before us."

L.3: And Pharaoh said to his brothers, "What is your occupation?" And they said to Pharaoh, "Your servants are shepherds, both we and our fathers."

R.3: Pharaoh asked them, "What is your work?" They said, "We are shepherds. Our fathers were shepherds too."

decisions.choice: shepherds: they name their trade plainly
decisions.reason: Joseph had told them to say they kept livestock (46:34). They answer with the word "shepherds", which Joseph himself had used (46:32). They do not hide what they are.

decisions.choice: We
decisions.reason: Calling oneself "your servant" was the polite way to speak to a superior. Readable uses "we"; Literal and Balanced keep the courtesy.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֗ה לָג֣וּר בָּאָרֶץ֮ בָּאנוּ֒ כִּי־אֵ֣ין מִרְעֶ֗ה לַצֹּאן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־כָבֵ֥ד הָרָעָ֖ב בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וְעַתָּ֛ה יֵֽשְׁבוּ־נָ֥א עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ גֹּֽשֶׁן׃
records.gloss: And they said to Pharaoh, to sojourn in the land we have come, for there is no pasture for the flock which [belongs] to your servants, for heavy [is] the famine in [the] land of Canaan; and now, let dwell, please, your servants in [the] land of Goshen.
pieces: They went on, "We have come to live in this country as foreigners for a while. The famine weighs hard on Canaan, and there is no pasture left there for the flocks your servants keep. Now please let your servants make their home in the land of Goshen."

L.4: And they said to Pharaoh, "We have come to sojourn in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants' flocks, for the famine is heavy in the land of Canaan. So now, please let your servants live in the land of Goshen."

R.4: They said, "We have come to stay in your country for a time. There is no grass for our animals in Canaan, because the famine there is very bad. So please let us live in Goshen."

decisions.choice: to sojourn: to live as foreigners
decisions.reason: Gur means to live in a land as a resident foreigner, without the rights of a citizen or a claim to the land. God had told Abraham that his descendants would be foreigners in a land not their own (15:13).

decisions.choice: the famine is heavy: severe
decisions.reason: A "heavy" famine is one that presses hard on the land (12:10; 43:1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֔ה אֶל־יוֹסֵ֖ף לֵאמֹ֑ר אָבִ֥יךָ וְאַחֶ֖יךָ בָּ֥אוּ אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Pharaoh to Joseph, saying, your father and your brothers have come to you.
pieces: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Your father and your brothers have come to you.

L.5: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Your father and your brothers have come to you.

R.5: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Your father and brothers have come to you.

decisions.choice: the order of verses 5-6, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: Pharaoh first grants Goshen, then the arrival of Jacob is told, then Pharaoh offers the best of the land (Septuagint)
decisions.reason: In the Septuagint, Pharaoh first answers the brothers' request with the words about Goshen and capable men, then a sentence tells that Jacob and his sons came to Joseph and that Pharaoh heard of it, and only then does Pharaoh speak these words. The sense is the same. The Hebrew order is followed.

records.source: אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לְפָנֶ֣יךָ הִ֔וא בְּמֵיטַ֣ב הָאָ֔רֶץ הוֹשֵׁ֥ב אֶת־אָבִ֖יךָ וְאֶת־אַחֶ֑יךָ יֵשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֔שֶׁן וְאִם־יָדַ֗עְתָּ וְיֶשׁ־בָּם֙ אַנְשֵׁי־חַ֔יִל וְשַׂמְתָּ֛ם שָׂרֵ֥י מִקְנֶ֖ה עַל־אֲשֶׁר־לִֽי׃
records.gloss: [The] land of Egypt before you it [is]; in [the] best of the land settle your father and your brothers; let them dwell in [the] land of Goshen; and if you know [that] there are among them men of ability, you will appoint them overseers of livestock over what [is] mine.
pieces: The whole land of Egypt is open to you. Give your father and brothers a home in the best part of the country; they may live in Goshen. And if there are capable men among them that you know of, make them chief herdsmen over the livestock that is mine."

L.6: The land of Egypt is before you. Settle your father and your brothers in the best of the land; let them live in the land of Goshen. And if you know any capable men among them, appoint them chiefs over my livestock."

R.6: All of Egypt is yours to choose from. Give your father and brothers the best part of the land. They can live in Goshen. And if any of them are very good at their work, make them the managers of my own herds."

decisions.choice: the land is before you: it is at your disposal
decisions.reason: To set a land "before" someone is to let him choose freely in it, as Abram offered Lot (13:9) and Abimelech offered Abraham (20:15).

decisions.choice: men of ability: capable men
decisions.reason: Chayil is strength, ability and worth. Pharaoh means men skilled and reliable enough to be trusted with the royal herds.

records.source: וַיָּבֵ֤א יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־יַֽעֲקֹ֣ב אָבִ֔יו וַיַּֽעֲמִדֵ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־פַּרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And brought Joseph Jacob his father and stood him before Pharaoh; and blessed Jacob Pharaoh.
pieces: Joseph then brought in his father Jacob and had him stand before Pharaoh, and Jacob gave Pharaoh his blessing.

L.7: And Joseph brought in Jacob his father and set him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.

R.7: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob to meet Pharaoh. Jacob asked God to bless Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: Jacob blessed Pharaoh: the old shepherd blesses the king
decisions.reason: Barakh can be used of a greeting, but a greeting given as a blessing, calling on God's favor. The old herdsman, a foreigner seeking refuge, blesses the ruler of Egypt. God had promised that through Abraham's family all the families of the earth would be blessed (12:3).

decisions.choice: asked God to bless
decisions.reason: To bless someone is to call on God to do him good; Readable says so plainly.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֑ב כַּמָּ֕ה יְמֵ֖י שְׁנֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Pharaoh to Jacob, how many [are the] days of [the] years of your life?
pieces: Pharaoh asked Jacob, "How many years have you lived?"

L.8: And Pharaoh said to Jacob, "How many are the days of the years of your life?"

R.8: Pharaoh asked Jacob, "How old are you?"

decisions.choice: the days of the years of your life: your lifetime
decisions.reason: A full, formal way of asking someone's age. Jacob takes up the phrase and repeats it in his answer.

decisions.choice: how many years have you lived
alternatives: how many are the days of the years of your life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable shorten the formal phrase; Literal keeps it.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵ֣י מְגוּרַ֔י שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָ֑ה מְעַ֣ט וְרָעִ֗ים הָיוּ֙ יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵ֣י חַיַּ֔י וְלֹ֣א הִשִּׂ֗יגוּ אֶת־יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י אֲבֹתַ֔י בִּימֵ֖י מְגוּרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Jacob to Pharaoh, [the] days of [the] years of my sojournings [are] 130 years; few and evil have been [the] days of [the] years of my life, and they have not reached [the] days of [the] years of [the] lives of my fathers in [the] days of their sojournings.
pieces: Jacob replied, "I have lived as a foreigner for 130 years. My years have been few and hard, and they fall short of the years my fathers lived as foreigners."

L.9: And Jacob said to Pharaoh, "The days of the years of my sojourning are 130 years. Few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their sojourning."

R.9: Jacob said, "I have been moving from place to place for 130 years. My life has been short and full of trouble. I have not lived as long as my father and grandfather did."

decisions.choice: my sojourning: my life as a foreigner
decisions.reason: Magur is the life of a resident foreigner, related to gur in verse 4. Abraham, Isaac and Jacob lived in Canaan without owning it; Abraham's only land was a grave (23:4). Hebrews 11:13 says they confessed they were strangers and exiles on the earth.

decisions.choice: few and evil: short and hard
decisions.reason: Ra here is not moral evil but trouble and hardship. Jacob has known exile, deceit, the death of Rachel and the long loss of Joseph.

decisions.choice: not reached the years of my fathers
decisions.reason: Abraham lived 175 years (25:7) and Isaac 180 (35:28). Jacob will die at 147 (47:28).

decisions.choice: my father and grandfather
decisions.reason: The fathers are Isaac and Abraham; Readable names them as father and grandfather.

records.source: וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיֵּצֵ֖א מִלִּפְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And blessed Jacob Pharaoh and went out from before Pharaoh.
pieces: Jacob blessed Pharaoh again as he took his leave.

L.10: And Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from Pharaoh's presence.

R.10: Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh again and left.

decisions.choice: blessed: a farewell blessing
decisions.reason: Jacob blesses Pharaoh both when he comes in (verse 7) and when he leaves, as greetings and farewells were spoken as blessings.

records.source: וַיּוֹשֵׁ֣ב יוֹסֵף֮ אֶת־אָבִ֣יו וְאֶת־אֶחָיו֒ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֤ם אֲחֻזָּה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּמֵיטַ֥ב הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ רַעְמְסֵ֑ס כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה פַרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And settled Joseph his father and his brothers, and gave to them a possession in [the] land of Egypt, in [the] best of the land, in [the] land of Rameses, as had commanded Pharaoh.
pieces: Joseph gave his father and brothers a home in Egypt, granting them land of their own in the finest part of the country, the region of Rameses, just as Pharaoh had said.

L.11: And Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.

R.11: Joseph found a place for his father and brothers to live in Egypt. He gave them land in the best part of the country, the area around Rameses. That is what Pharaoh had told him to do.

decisions.choice: possession: land held as one's own
decisions.reason: Achuzzah is a landholding. It is the word used for the burial ground Abraham bought in Canaan (23:4, 9, 20). In Canaan the family owns only a grave; in Egypt they are given land.

decisions.choice: the land of Rameses: the area of Goshen
decisions.reason: Rameses was the name of a later city in this region, built by Israelite slaves (Exodus 1:11) and the starting point of the exodus (Exodus 12:37). The narrator uses the name his readers knew for the district.

records.source: וַיְכַלְכֵּ֤ל יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־אָבִ֣יו וְאֶת־אֶחָ֔יו וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑יו לֶ֖חֶם לְפִ֥י הַטָּֽף׃
records.gloss: And provided Joseph his father and his brothers and all [the] household of his father [with] food according to [the] mouth of the little ones.
pieces: Joseph fed his father, his brothers and all his father's household, giving each family food in proportion to its little ones.

L.12: And Joseph provided his father and his brothers and all his father's household with food, according to the number of their little ones.

R.12: Joseph gave food to his father, his brothers and all their families. Each family got enough for all its children.

decisions.choice: according to the mouth of the little ones: by the number of their children
decisions.reason: Lefi, "according to the mouth of", usually means "in proportion to". Each family received food by the number of its dependents, the youngest included.

decisions.choice: according to the number of
decisions.reason: Literal gives the meaning of the idiom, which would mislead if kept word for word.

records.source: וְלֶ֤חֶם אֵין֙ בְּכָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי־כָבֵ֥ד הָרָעָ֖ב מְאֹ֑ד וַתֵּ֜לַהּ אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ וְאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן מִפְּנֵ֖י הָרָעָֽב׃
records.gloss: And food there was not in all the land, for heavy [was] the famine very; and languished [the] land of Egypt and [the] land of Canaan because of the famine.
pieces: Food was gone from the whole land, so cruel had the famine become, and both Egypt and Canaan grew faint under it.

L.13: Now there was no food in all the land, for the famine was very heavy, and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished because of the famine.

R.13: Soon there was no food anywhere, because the famine was very bad. The people in Egypt and Canaan were weak from hunger.

decisions.choice: languished: grew faint, was exhausted
decisions.reason: The verb, found only here, describes the land and its people worn out by hunger.

decisions.choice: the people in Egypt and Canaan
alternatives: the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan
decisions.reason: The lands stand for the people who live in them; Readable says so.

records.source: וַיְלַקֵּ֣ט יוֹסֵ֗ף אֶת־כָּל־הַכֶּ֨סֶף֙ הַנִּמְצָ֤א בְאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ וּבְאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן בַּשֶּׁ֖בֶר אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֣ם שֹׁבְרִ֑ים וַיָּבֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת־הַכֶּ֖סֶף בֵּ֥יתָה פַרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And gathered up Joseph all the money found in [the] land of Egypt and in [the] land of Canaan for the grain which they were buying; and brought Joseph the money to [the] house of Pharaoh.
pieces: As people bought grain, Joseph took in all the money there was in Egypt and in Canaan, and he deposited it in Pharaoh's palace.

L.14: And Joseph gathered up all the silver that was found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they were buying, and Joseph brought the silver into Pharaoh's house.

R.14: People bought grain with their money until Joseph had collected all the money in Egypt and Canaan. He brought the money to Pharaoh's palace.

decisions.choice: silver: money weighed out
decisions.reason: Kesef is silver, the money of the time. There were no coins yet; silver was weighed out for payment (23:16).

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "silver"; Balanced and Readable say "money" because the silver here is the price paid for grain, as in 44:1.

records.source: וַיִּתֹּ֣ם הַכֶּ֗סֶף מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֮ וּמֵאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַעַן֒ וַיָּבֹאוּ֩ כָל־מִצְרַ֨יִם אֶל־יוֹסֵ֤ף לֵאמֹר֙ הָֽבָה־לָּ֣נוּ לֶ֔חֶם וְלָ֥מָּה נָמ֖וּת נֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י אָפֵ֖ס כָּֽסֶף׃
records.gloss: And was finished the money from [the] land of Egypt and from [the] land of Canaan, and came all Egypt to Joseph saying, give to us food; and why should we die before you? for has come to an end [the] money.
pieces: When the money in Egypt and Canaan ran out, the Egyptians all came to Joseph. "Give us food," they pleaded. "Must we die in front of you? We have no money left."

L.15: And when the silver was spent in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, "Give us food! Why should we die before you? For the silver is gone."

R.15: When all the money in Egypt and Canaan was spent, the Egyptians came to Joseph. They said, "Give us food! Do not let us die right here in front of you. We have no money left."

decisions.choice: why should we die before you?: a plea, not a question
decisions.reason: The question is an appeal: surely Joseph will not stand by and watch them starve.

decisions.choice: Do not let us die
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the plea it expresses.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ הָב֣וּ מִקְנֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם בְּמִקְנֵיכֶ֑ם אִם־אָפֵ֖ס כָּֽסֶף׃
records.gloss: And said Joseph, give your livestock, and I will give to you for your livestock, if has come to an end [the] money.
pieces: "If your money is used up," Joseph answered, "hand over your livestock, and I will give you food in return for them."

L.16: And Joseph said, "Give [me] your livestock, and I will give you [food] for your livestock, if [your] silver is gone."

R.16: Joseph said, "If you have no money, bring me your animals. I will give you food in exchange for them."

decisions.choice: food
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "I will give to you"; food is meant. Literal brackets the word.

records.source: וַיָּבִ֣יאוּ אֶת־מִקְנֵיהֶם֮ אֶל־יוֹסֵף֒ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָהֶם֩ יוֹסֵ֨ף לֶ֜חֶם בַּסּוּסִ֗ים וּבְמִקְנֵ֥ה הַצֹּ֛אן וּבְמִקְנֵ֥ה הַבָּקָ֖ר וּבַחֲמֹרִ֑ים וַיְנַהֲלֵ֤ם בַּלֶּ֨חֶם֙ בְּכָל־מִקְנֵהֶ֔ם בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִֽוא׃
records.gloss: And they brought their livestock to Joseph, and gave to them Joseph food for the horses and for the livestock of the flocks and for the livestock of the herds and for the donkeys; and he provided them with food for all their livestock in that year.
pieces: The people led their animals to Joseph, and he traded them food for horses, for sheep and goats, for cattle and for donkeys. Through that whole year he sustained them with food, taking all their livestock in return.

L.17: So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them food in exchange for the horses, the flocks, the herds and the donkeys. And he provided for them with food in exchange for all their livestock that year.

R.17: So the people brought their animals to Joseph. He gave them food for their horses, sheep, goats, cattle and donkeys. That year he fed them in exchange for all their animals.

decisions.choice: provided for them: led them like a shepherd
decisions.reason: Nahal is used of a shepherd leading his flock to water and caring for it (Psalm 23:2; Isaiah 40:11). Joseph sees the people through the year.

decisions.choice: sheep and goats
decisions.reason: Tson means a flock of small animals, sheep and goats together.

records.source: וַתִּתֹּם֮ הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִוא֒ וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ אֵלָ֜יו בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשֵּׁנִ֗ית וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ לֹֽא־נְכַחֵ֣ד מֵֽאֲדֹנִ֔י כִּ֚י אִם־תַּ֣ם הַכֶּ֔סֶף וּמִקְנֵ֥ה הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֑י לֹ֤א נִשְׁאַר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י בִּלְתִּ֥י אִם־גְּוִיָּתֵ֖נוּ וְאַדְמָתֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And was finished that year, and they came to him in the second year and said to him, we will not hide from my lord that, since has been finished the money and the livestock of the animals [is] to my lord, there is not left before my lord except our bodies and our land.
pieces: That year came to an end, and in the next they came to him again. "My lord," they said, "we will not pretend otherwise: the money is spent, and the animals are already yours. We have nothing left to offer my lord but ourselves and our land.

L.18: When that year was ended, they came to him in the second year and said to him, "We will not hide from my lord that our silver is spent, and the herds of livestock are my lord's. Nothing is left before my lord but our bodies and our land.

R.18: When that year was over, the people came to Joseph again. They said, "Sir, we cannot hide the truth from you. Our money is gone, and our animals belong to you now. All we have left are our bodies and our land.

decisions.choice: the second year: the following year
alternatives: the second year of the famine
decisions.reason: "The second year" counts from the year just ended, when they gave their livestock. It is not the second year of the famine, which had begun earlier (45:6).

decisions.choice: our bodies: ourselves
decisions.reason: Gewiyyah is the body, often a dead one. The people have nothing left to offer but themselves and their fields.

decisions.choice: ourselves
decisions.reason: Balanced says "ourselves"; Literal and Readable keep the starker "bodies".

records.source: לָ֧מָּה נָמ֣וּת לְעֵינֶ֗יךָ גַּם־אֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ גַּ֣ם אַדְמָתֵ֔נוּ קְנֵֽה־אֹתָ֥נוּ וְאֶת־אַדְמָתֵ֖נוּ בַּלָּ֑חֶם וְנִֽהְיֶ֞ה אֲנַ֤חְנוּ וְאַדְמָתֵ֨נוּ֙ עֲבָדִ֣ים לְפַרְעֹ֔ה וְתֶן־זֶ֗רַע וְנִֽחְיֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א נָמ֔וּת וְהָאֲדָמָ֖ה לֹ֥א תֵשָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for food, and we will be, we and our land, slaves to Pharaoh; and give seed so that we may live and not die, and the land will not be desolate.
pieces: Why let us die before your eyes, our land as well as ourselves? Purchase us and our land in return for food. We will be Pharaoh's slaves and our land will be his. Give us seed, so that we can live and not die, and the soil will not go to ruin."

L.19: Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for food, and we with our land will be slaves to Pharaoh. And give [us] seed, so that we may live and not die, and the land may not become desolate."

R.19: Do not let us die here in front of you! Do not let our land be ruined! Buy us and our land, and give us food in return. We will be Pharaoh's slaves, and our land will belong to him. Give us seed to plant, so that we can live and not die, and the fields will not become a desert."

decisions.choice: slaves to Pharaoh: bound to the crown
decisions.reason: Eved is a slave, one owned by another. Here the people become bound to Pharaoh and work his land, paying him a fifth of the harvest (verse 24). It is a dependent status the people themselves ask for to stay alive. Later Israel itself will be enslaved in Egypt (Exodus 1:11-14).

decisions.choice: the land will not be desolate: the fields will not lie waste
decisions.reason: Without seed to sow, the farmland would be abandoned. People and land live or die together.

decisions.choice: Do not let us die here in front of you
alternatives: Why should we die before your eyes
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the plea it expresses.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" at every level: the people sell themselves to Pharaoh for food (m1), so the style guide keeps the word for people bought.

records.source: וַיִּ֨קֶן יוֹסֵ֜ף אֶת־כָּל־אַדְמַ֤ת מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לְפַרְעֹ֔ה כִּֽי־מָכְר֤וּ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ אִ֣ישׁ שָׂדֵ֔הוּ כִּֽי־חָזַ֥ק עֲלֵהֶ֖ם הָרָעָ֑ב וַתְּהִ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ לְפַרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And bought Joseph all [the] land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for sold [the] Egyptians each his field, for was severe upon them the famine; and became the land Pharaoh's.
pieces: So Joseph acquired all the farmland of Egypt for Pharaoh. The famine pressed so hard on the Egyptians that every one of them sold his field, and the land passed to Pharaoh.

L.20: So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for the Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine was severe on them. And the land became Pharaoh's.

R.20: The famine was so bad that every Egyptian sold his field. In this way Joseph bought all the land in Egypt for Pharaoh, and it all became Pharaoh's.

records.source: וְאֶ֨ת־הָעָ֔ם הֶעֱבִ֥יר אֹת֖וֹ לֶעָרִ֑ים מִקְצֵ֥ה גְבוּל־מִצְרַ֖יִם וְעַד־קָצֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And the people he moved them to [the] cities from [the] end of [the] border of Egypt and to its end.
pieces: The people he relocated to the cities, throughout Egypt from border to border.

L.21: And as for the people, he moved them to the cities from one end of the territory of Egypt to the other.

R.21: Joseph moved the people into the cities, all across Egypt from one end to the other.

decisions.choice: he moved them to the cities, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: he made them slaves (Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads he'evir ... le'arim, "he moved ... to the cities". The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint read he'evid ... la'avadim, "he made ... slaves", which differs mainly by one similar-looking letter and matches the people's offer (verses 19, 25). The Hebrew text is followed; moving people to the cities may mean bringing them near the grain stored there (41:48).

records.source: רַ֛ק אַדְמַ֥ת הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים לֹ֣א קָנָ֑ה כִּי֩ חֹ֨ק לַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים מֵאֵ֣ת פַּרְעֹ֗ה וְאָֽכְל֤וּ אֶת־חֻקָּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן לָהֶם֙ פַּרְעֹ֔ה עַל־כֵּ֕ן לֹ֥א מָכְר֖וּ אֶת־אַדְמָתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Only [the] land of the priests he did not buy, for an allowance [was] to the priests from Pharaoh, and they ate their allowance which gave to them Pharaoh; therefore they did not sell their land.
pieces: Only the priests' land he did not buy, because the priests had a fixed share of food from Pharaoh and lived on what Pharaoh allotted them. So they kept their land.

L.22: Only the land of the priests he did not buy, for the priests had a fixed allowance from Pharaoh and lived on the allowance that Pharaoh gave them; therefore they did not sell their land.

R.22: But Joseph did not buy the land that belonged to the priests. Pharaoh gave the priests a set amount of food, and they lived on it. So they could keep their land.

decisions.choice: allowance: a fixed portion
decisions.reason: Choq is something fixed or set: a fixed share of food here, and a fixed rule in verse 26. The priests, fed by Pharaoh, did not need to sell their land.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם הֵן֩ קָנִ֨יתִי אֶתְכֶ֥ם הַיּ֛וֹם וְאֶת־אַדְמַתְכֶ֖ם לְפַרְעֹ֑ה הֵֽא־לָכֶ֣ם זֶ֔רַע וּזְרַעְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־הָאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Joseph to the people, here, I have bought you this day and your land for Pharaoh; here for you [is] seed, and you will sow the land.
pieces: Joseph told the people, "As of today, you and your land belong to Pharaoh; I have bought them for him. Here is seed. Go and sow your fields.

L.23: Then Joseph said to the people, "Look, I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh. Here is seed for you, and you shall sow the land.

R.23: Joseph told the people, "You and your land now belong to Pharaoh. I bought them for him today. Here is seed. Plant it in your fields.

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ בַּתְּבוּאֹ֔ת וּנְתַתֶּ֥ם חֲמִישִׁ֖ית לְפַרְעֹ֑ה וְאַרְבַּ֣ע הַיָּדֹ֡ת יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶם֩ לְזֶ֨רַע הַשָּׂדֶ֧ה וּֽלְאָכְלְכֶ֛ם וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּבָתֵּיכֶ֖ם וְלֶאֱכֹ֥ל לְטַפְּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And it will be at the harvests, and you will give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four of the hands will be to you for seed of the field and for your food and for those who [are] in your households and to eat for your little ones.
pieces: At harvest time you will hand over one fifth to Pharaoh. Four parts out of five will be yours to use as seed for the fields and to feed yourselves, everyone in your homes and your little ones."

L.24: And at the harvests you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts shall be yours, as seed for the field and as food for you and for those in your households, and as food for your little ones."

R.24: When you harvest your crops, give one part out of every five to Pharaoh. You may keep the other four parts. Use them as seed for your fields and as food for your families and your children."

decisions.choice: a fifth: the share for Pharaoh
decisions.reason: A fifth of the harvest is the same share Joseph had collected in the seven good years (41:34). The people keep four fifths for seed and food.

decisions.choice: four of the hands: four parts
decisions.reason: "Hands" here means shares or portions, as in 43:34, where Benjamin's portion was five "hands" larger.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ הֶחֱיִתָ֑נוּ נִמְצָא־חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י וְהָיִ֥ינוּ עֲבָדִ֖ים לְפַרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And they said, you have kept us alive; may we find favor in [the] eyes of my lord, and we will be slaves to Pharaoh.
pieces: They replied, "You have kept us alive! Let us find favor with you, my lord, and we will be Pharaoh's slaves."

L.25: And they said, "You have saved our lives! May we find favor in the eyes of my lord, and we will be slaves to Pharaoh."

R.25: The people said, "You have saved our lives! Sir, please be kind to us, and we will be Pharaoh's slaves."

decisions.choice: may we find favor in my lord's eyes: a polite thanks and request
decisions.reason: The phrase asks for the superior's goodwill and also expresses thanks for it. The people accept the terms gladly, since they have been kept alive.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" at every level: the people give themselves to Pharaoh in exchange for food (verse 19), so the style guide keeps the word for people bought.

records.source: וַיָּ֣שֶׂם אֹתָ֣הּ יוֹסֵ֡ף לְחֹק֩ עַד־הַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה עַל־אַדְמַ֥ת מִצְרַ֛יִם לְפַרְעֹ֖ה לַחֹ֑מֶשׁ רַ֞ק אַדְמַ֤ת הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ לְבַדָּ֔ם לֹ֥א הָיְתָ֖ה לְפַרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And established it Joseph as a statute until this day over [the] land of Egypt: to Pharaoh, a fifth. Only [the] land of the priests alone did not become Pharaoh's.
pieces: Joseph laid this down as a rule for the land of Egypt, and it holds to this day: Pharaoh receives a fifth. The priests' land was the only land that never came to belong to Pharaoh.

L.26: And Joseph made it a statute concerning the land of Egypt, to this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth. Only the land of the priests alone did not become Pharaoh's.

R.26: Joseph made this a law in Egypt, and it is still the law today: one fifth of the crops belongs to Pharaoh. Only the priests' land did not become Pharaoh's.

decisions.choice: statute: a fixed rule
decisions.reason: Choq, the word used for the priests' fixed allowance in verse 22, here means a fixed rule. The rule stood "to this day", in the time of the narrator.

records.source: וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֑שֶׁן וַיֵּאָחֲז֣וּ בָ֔הּ וַיִּפְר֥וּ וַיִּרְבּ֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And dwelt Israel in [the] land of Egypt, in [the] land of Goshen; and they acquired property in it and were fruitful and multiplied exceedingly.
pieces: Israel made its home in Egypt, in the land of Goshen. They gained land there, were fruitful, and multiplied greatly.

L.27: And Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen. And they gained possessions in it, and were fruitful and multiplied greatly.

R.27: So the people of Israel lived in Egypt, in the land of Goshen. They got land of their own there. They had many children, and their numbers grew very large.

decisions.choice: Israel: the family as a people
decisions.reason: The verb "lived" is singular, but the verbs that follow are plural: Israel is now the whole family, becoming a people.

decisions.choice: fruitful and multiplied: the blessing of creation
decisions.reason: The words echo God's first blessing on humankind (1:28) and his promise to Jacob (35:11). Exodus 1:7 takes them up again as the people fill the land of Egypt.

records.source: וַיְחִ֤י יַעֲקֹב֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם שְׁבַ֥ע עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י יְמֵֽי־יַעֲקֹב֙ שְׁנֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And lived Jacob in [the] land of Egypt seventeen years; and were [the] days of Jacob, [the] years of his life, 147 years.
pieces: Jacob lived on in Egypt for seventeen more years; his whole life came to 147 years.

L.28: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years. So the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were 147 years.

R.28: Jacob lived in Egypt for seventeen years. He lived to be 147 years old.

decisions.choice: seventeen years: years given back
decisions.reason: Joseph was seventeen when his father lost him (37:2). Now Jacob has seventeen years with him in Egypt.

records.source: וַיִּקְרְב֣וּ יְמֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֘ללָמוּת֒ וַיִּקְרָ֣א׀לִבְנ֣וֹ לְיוֹסֵ֗ף וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אִם־נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ שִֽׂים־נָ֥א יָדְךָ֖ תַּ֣חַת יְרֵכִ֑י וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ עִמָּדִי֙ חֶ֣סֶד וֶאֱמֶ֔ת אַל־נָ֥א תִקְבְּרֵ֖נִי בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And drew near [the] days of Israel to die, and he called his son Joseph and said to him, if please I have found favor in your eyes, put please your hand under my thigh, and you will do with me loyalty and faithfulness; please do not bury me in Egypt.
pieces: When Israel's death was near, he summoned his son Joseph. "If you hold me in your favor," he said, "put your hand under my thigh and pledge me your loyalty and faithfulness. Do not bury me in Egypt.

L.29: When the time drew near for Israel to die, he called his son Joseph and said to him, "If now I have found favor in your eyes, put your hand under my thigh, and deal with me in loyalty and faithfulness. Please do not bury me in Egypt,

R.29: When Israel knew he would soon die, he called for his son Joseph. He said to him, "Please do this for me. Put your hand under my thigh as a sign of a solemn promise. Promise to be loyal and faithful to me. Do not bury me in Egypt.

decisions.choice: hand under my thigh: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: Abraham's servant swore an oath in the same way (24:2, 9). The thigh stands for a man's power to father children, his line of descendants (46:26), so the oath is made with the family's future as witness.

decisions.choice: loyalty and faithfulness: true and lasting kindness
decisions.reason: Chesed is loyal love that keeps faith with a bond; emet is faithfulness, reliability. Together they mean kindness that can be relied on to the end (24:27, 49).

decisions.choice: as a sign of a solemn promise
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the gesture meant.

records.source: וְשָֽׁכַבְתִּי֙ עִם־אֲבֹתַ֔י וּנְשָׂאתַ֨נִי֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וּקְבַרְתַּ֖נִי בִּקְבֻרָתָ֑ם וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אָנֹכִ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה כִדְבָרֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And I will lie with my fathers, and you will carry me from Egypt and bury me in their grave. And he said, I will do according to your word.
pieces: When I lie down with my fathers, take me up out of Egypt and lay me in their grave." "I will do what you have asked," Joseph said.

L.30: but when I lie down with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burial place." And he said, "I will do as you have said."

R.30: After I die, carry my body out of Egypt. Bury me in the grave of my ancestors." Joseph said, "I will do what you ask."

decisions.choice: lie down with my fathers: die
decisions.reason: To lie down with one's fathers is to die and join one's ancestors in death. Their grave is the cave of Machpelah, where Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah and Leah were buried (23:19; 25:9; 49:29-32).

decisions.choice: Joseph
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Joseph as the speaker.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִשָּֽׁבְעָה֙ לִ֔י וַיִּשָּׁבַ֖ע ל֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הַמִּטָּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And he said, swear to me; and he swore to him; and bowed Israel at [the] head of the bed.
pieces: "Swear it to me," Israel said, and Joseph swore it. Then Israel bowed down at the head of his bed.

L.31: And he said, "Swear to me." And he swore to him. Then Israel bowed down at the head of the bed.

R.31: Israel said, "Make a promise to me." So Joseph promised him. Then Israel bowed low at the head of his bed.

decisions.choice: the head of the bed, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: the top of his staff (Septuagint; Hebrews 11:21)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words for "bed" (mittah) and "staff" (matteh) are written with the same consonants. The Septuagint read "staff": Israel bowed "upon the top of his staff", and Hebrews 11:21 quotes it. The Hebrew text, which reads "bed", is followed; Jacob is old and near death (48:2).

decisions.choice: Israel bowed down: in worship, or to Joseph
decisions.reason: Hishtachavah is to bow low. Jacob may bow in worship, thanking God that his burial in the promised land is secured, or bow to Joseph, as Joseph's dream had foretold (37:9-10).

decisions.choice: Israel ... Joseph
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speakers.
